card.title: Metallic Bonding and Properties of Metallic Solids

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The metallic bond is the crystal-scale bargain: metal atoms, with low ionisation energies, surrender their valence electrons into a **delocalised sea** that electrostatically binds the fixed cation lattice — non-directional, collective, and forgiving.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - mp trend (period 3 metals): Na 98 < Mg 650 < Al 660 °C - Band gaps: conductor ≈ 0; Si ≈ 1 eV; diamond ≈ 5.5 eV - Conductivity ranking: Ag > Cu > Au > Al

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Conduction is electron flow, not ion flow:** in a copper wire the Cu²⁺-core lattice never migrates; in molten NaCl it is the ions that carry current — keep the two mechanisms separate.  ·  **"Electron sea" is a model, not a photograph:** it is the elementary picture; band theory is its quantum refinement — cite both for full marks on "explain metallic bonding".

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Specialized insight for 11 metallic bonding and properties of metallic solids.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Brass and steel*** — Zn substitutes for Cu; C squeezes between Fe atoms — both distort the lattice just enough to block slip planes, hardening the metal without destroying the bond.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Property → mechanism map: conducts → electron sea; malleable → non-directional bond; lustrous → re-emission; high mp → cation charge × electron count. Band gaps: metal 0, Si 1 eV, diamond 5.5 eV.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The sliding test is the master comparison: metal layers slide and stay bonded; ionic layers slide and repel apart. One geometric fact explains malleability vs brittleness across two entire bonding types.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Metallic bond = cation lattice + delocalised valence electrons; non-directional. Explains: conduction (mobile electrons), thermal conduction, lustre (re-emission), malleability/ductility (layers slide, sea re-adjusts — ionic crystals shatter instead), high mp trend Na < Mg < Al.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Mercury is liquid at room temperature (29.8 °C mp) — the only metal — used in thermometers and barometers precisely because its electron sea still conducts while the lattice barely coheres.

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Bond That Bends Instead of Breaks Metals conduct, gleam, bend and hammer without shattering — behaviour no ionic or covalent model can explain. Common Confusions **The cations do not move during conduction:** only the electron sea flows; the lattice stays fixed. (In electrolysis the *ions* move — different process.)  ·  **Metallic bonds are not covalent:** no localized shared pairs between specific atoms — the electrons are collective property of the crystal.
